Photo by Agata Bogucka, NLR 91973 2 https://dx.doi.org/10.1021/acs.iecr.5c02169 14 | Advanced Computing Annual Report 2025 Advanced Computing Annual Report 2025 | 15 Optimizing Cooling for AI Data Centers The Cooling Operations Optimized for Leaps in Energy, Reliability, and Carbon Hyperefficiency for Information Processing Systems (COOLERCHIPS) project, funded by ARPA-E, progresses energy-efficient data center design by rethinking cooling for increasingly power-dense AI hardware. As AI chips push beyond traditional thermal limits, cooling becomes a mission-critical bottleneck: essential for performance and reliability, yet historically one of the most energy-intensive parts of a data center. COOLERCHIPS uses HPC to scale two-phase flow thermal simulations from chip level to full data center architecture, exploring designs that could reduce cooling energy consumption to under 5% of the total information technology load—an order-of-magnitude improvement over today’s systems. Leveraging Kestrel’s large-scale simulation capabilities, researchers model diverse operating conditions, identify optimal working points for chip- and server-level cooling loops, and generate rich datasets to train ML models that accurately predict two-phase heat transfer behavior. These ML models are integrated to create a digital twin of the data center rack, enabling optimized heat transfer under dynamic load conditions while beneficially minimizing power usage effectiveness (PUE). This digital twin framework directly informs cooling system design and control strategies for the next generation of AI chips, servers, and racks, enabling more efficiently cooled data centers.
